question.text: Which of the alkaline earth metal halides given below is essentially covalent in nature?

solution.text: <math><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi><msup><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">e</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo>+</mo></mrow></msup></math>  cation is very small in size and in terms of Fajan's rules brings about polarization of electronic cloud of anion  <math><mo>(</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><msup><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">l</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>-</mo></mrow></msup><mo>)</mo></math>  i.e.  <math><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">e</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">l</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub></math>  is covalent in nature.
